speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a dermatological condition with potential oncologic implications; can you tell me what the lesion looks like and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the Penis and Left Middle Finger.

The patient's history of heavy smoking, non-healing crusted lesions in sun-exposed (finger) and high-risk (penile) areas, and failure of previous treatments strongly suggests cutaneous SCC. Given the potential for metastasis, I will request a biopsy and staging imaging.
